summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted for shortness of breath and fluid overload. He had gained weight and was unable to lie flat due to orthopnea. Initial peritoneal dialysis provided no relief, so he underwent hemodialysis, which removed 4 liters of fluid and significantly improved his symptoms. His hyperkalemia resolved with treatment, and peritoneal fluid analysis showed no infection. The peritoneal catheter was in the correct position, but due to ongoing difficulties, the decision was made to transition to hemodialysis temporarily. His prolonged QT interval prompted discontinuation of trazodone. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged for dialysis and medication management.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
